identity.title: Signatures of Young Star Formation Activity within Two Parsecs of Sgr A*

paper_type_evidence.quote: The water maser data are presented here for the first time; the rest of the data have already been either completely or partly published in the past

evidence.quote: the distance to the Galactic center of 8.5 kpc $\pm$10%
the distance to the Galactic center of 8.5 kpc $\pm$10%

question.value: Is there on-going star formation within ~2 pc of Sgr A*, as indicated by water masers, YSO SED fits, SiO clumps, ionized jet kinematics and radio dark clouds?

evidence.quote: We present radio and infrared observations indicating on-going star formation activity inside the $\sim2-5$ pc circumnuclear ring at the Galactic center.
we detect clumps of SiO (2-1) and (5-4) line emission in the ring based on CARMA and SMA observations
water masers (22.23419 GHz) within 2 pc of Sgr A\* with the Green Bank Telescope

angular_resolution.value: SiO (5-4) ALMA data of the ring interior only referenced from Yusef-Zadeh et al. 2013; SMA 3.6''x2.4'' used here

evidence.quote: with a spatial and spectral resolution of $3.6''\times2.4''$ and 2 km s$^{-1}$  respectively

provided.value: 22 GHz water maser observations, B-configuration, 2012 Feb 2

evidence.quote: Water maser observations were carried out with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA)[^1] in its B-configuration on February 2, 2012.
The SiO (2-1) line data were taken with the Combined Array for Research in Millimeter-wave Astronomy (CARMA)
We also used the SiO (5-4) line data taken with the Sub-Millimeter Array (SMA).
We used the published data obtained with the Very Large Telescope (VLT) at wavelengths ranging between 1.6 and 19.5 $\mu$m (Viehmann et al. 2006).
Sgr A West was observed in the \[Ne II\] (12.8$\mu$m) line with the high-resolution mid-infrared spectrograph TEXES on the NASA IRTF

what.value: ALMA SiO (5-4) detection of 11 clumps in ring interior

evidence.quote: ALMA observations of the interior of the molecular ring detected SiO (5-4) emission from 11 clumps (Yusef-Zadeh et al. 2013).
The data points for Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) fitting (see $\S3.2$) are taken from Table 1 of Viehmann et al. (2006)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Robitaille et al. (2006) grid of pre-computed YSO model SEDs

evidence.quote: We compare the sources’ SEDs to the Robitaille et al. (2006) large grid of pre-computed YSO model SEDs

flux_calibrator.value: 3C286 primary flux calibrator (VLA); NRAO530 gain and bandpass

evidence.quote: 3C286 was used as a primary flux calibrator and NRAO530 as the complex gain and bandpass calibrator.

continuum_subtraction.value: UVLSF in AIPS in the visibility plane

evidence.quote: Continuum subtraction in the visibility plane was carried out using the UVLSF task of AIPS
The rms noise in each channel map is about 2.8 mJy beam$^{-1}$.
We used the same technique that identified a population of YSO candidates toward the inner few hundred parsecs of the Galaxy

what.value: SMA SiO observations similar to earlier paper

evidence.quote: Details of these observations are very similar to the data presented in Martin et al. (2012)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA data reduction details and project code (only referenced from Yusef-Zadeh et al. 2013)

method.value: Fit VLT SEDs to Robitaille YSO model grid with linear regression fitter; well-fit if chi2/pt<3

evidence.quote: We identify well-fit models as those with a normalized $\chi^2$ per data point ($\chi^2/pt$) less than 3.

software: Robitaille et al. 2007 SED fitting tool

key_parameters.value: A_V 25-30 mag; distance 7.65-9.35 kpc; sources with >=4 fluxes

evidence.quote: We consider models with interstellar extinction ($A_{V}$) between 25 and 30 mag, and distance between 7.65 and 9.35 kpc

fitting.value: Parameters averaged over models with chi2/pt within chi2min+2

evidence.quote: averaging parameters of all YSO models that fit the source’s SED with $\chi^2/pt$ in a range between the $\chi^2/pt$ for the best-fitting model
The visual examination of the fits showed that the YSO model fits

method.value: Scale Kroupa IMF to Stage I YSO mass distribution, integrate 0.08-50 Msun, divide by lifetime

evidence.quote: scale the Kroupa (2001) initial mass function (IMF; $dN/dm \propto m^{-\alpha}$, m – a stellar mass) to match the peak of the distribution
Assuming a typical lifetime of the Stage I YSO of 10$^{5}$ years

method.value: Convolve CARMA and SMA to common resolution, Gaussian fit, uniform slab LVG with 5-4/2-1 ratio

evidence.quote: we first convolved the CARMA and SMA data to an identical resolution of $6.85''\times3.73''$ and then performed Gaussian fits to the sources

key_parameters.value: dust temperature 75 K, A_V 30, Tkin 50 and 150 K, FWHM 30 km/s

evidence.quote: a dust temperature of 75 K, 30 magnitudes of visual extinction and a dust extinction curve following Draine & Lee (1984)

used_for.value: VLA calibration and UVLSF continuum subtraction

evidence.quote: The data were calibrated in the usual manner using Astronomical Image Processing System (AIPS).
We detect 13 water masers concentrated toward the inner edge of the molecular ring.
only 19 out of 52 sources are well-fit by YSO models
the SFR within 1 pc of Sgr A\* is estimated to be $\sim$1$\times10^{-2}$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$
the total mass and the mass loss rate are $\sim0.5$   and $\sim5\times10^{-5}$   yr$^{-1}$, respectively

claims.hypothesis: Star formation is on-going within 2 pc of Sgr A*
claims.experiment: Water masers, SED fitting, SiO clumps, [Ne II] kinematics, radio dark clouds
claims.result: 13 masers, 19 YSO-fit sources, 26 SiO clumps, SiO bipolar outflow candidate, jet-like ionized ridge
claims.finding: Multiple lines of evidence support disk-based on-going star formation near Sgr A*

evidence.quote: We have presented five different lines of evidence in favor of on-going star formation near Sgr A\*.

limitations_admitted.value: SFR is only an order of magnitude estimate

evidence.quote: This is only an order magnitude estimate because of the small number statistics

referee_caveats_inferred: Water masers with multiple components may be OH/IR stars
ALMA data only inherited, not reanalysed

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: small to moderate (~tens of GB across VLA, CARMA, SMA)
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA role minor; many inputs from prior papers.
